name: Viceroy Hotels Ltd
title: Viceroy Hotels Ltd - 523796 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Hotel operator (Hyderabad Marriott/Courtyard, new Executive Apartments) with Q4 revenue +35% largely from acquisition; ADR softened in March, FY26 EBITDA margin 29.8%, and capex and debt are rising with no supply-discipline signal.

utilisation.quote: Q1-Q2, while it operates at 70% occupancy across the portfolio, at Q3-Q4, we can expect to be 80% and north of 80%.

capex.quote: We outlined a plan to invest 100 plus crores to renovate and upgrade existing properties in three phases.

triggers.quote: for a total consideration of around INR 215 crores

triggers.label: Q4 ADR softened in March
triggers.quote: ADR performance during the quarter reflected the relatively softer operating environment witnessed across the hospitality sector during March.

triggers.label: Madhapur Courtyard targeted FY29-FY30
triggers.quote: we would say we are targeting the opening date to be FY '29 or FY '30.

We are going to see a substantial twofold increase in the EBITDAs because of this addition.
we expect to give you a good outcome from next year.

summary.headline: Viceroy Hotels Q4 FY26 revenue rose 35.3% YoY to INR 49.5 crore, with EBITDA margin up 183 bps to 31.4%, aided by the Marriott Executive Apartments acquisition.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR 49.5 crore versus INR 36.6 crore a year earlier, and operating EBITDA rose 43.7% YoY to INR 15.6 crore. Growth was driven mainly by consolidation of Marriott Executive Apartments (75 rooms, acquired 1 January 2026), which contributed its first quarter. Management said March was softer on geopolitical tensions and the West Asia conflict, with ADR and occupancy moderating at the existing hotels. PAT fell to about INR 6 crore, which management attributed to higher depreciation and finance costs from renovation and acquisition debt, and to a deferred-tax benefit booked in the prior year.

financial_highlights.change: Down roughly 40% YoY per analyst question; management cited higher depreciation, finance cost and prior-year deferred tax credit

F&B revenue, Marriott and Courtyard (Q4 FY26)

financial_highlights.value: Room INR 9 crore; F&B INR 3.7 crore

segments.name: Marriott and Courtyard (Hyderabad, Tank Bund)
segments.commentary: Q4 combined ADR INR 7,605 (Marriott INR 7,423; Courtyard INR 8,010) and combined RevPAR INR 4,931, with softer occupancy in March. Full-year ADR grew 6.8% at Marriott and Courtyard, and FY26 Courtyard occupancy was 52.2% versus 72.6% earlier, which management attributed to renovation.

segments.name: Marriott Executive Apartments (Hyderabad, 75 rooms)
segments.commentary: First quarter of consolidation: ADR up 6.9% YoY to INR 16,578 and RevPAR up 3.2% YoY to INR 13,438, with room revenue INR 9 crore and F&B INR 3.7 crore. Room-led mix (about 64-65% rooms, 32-33% F&B) gives higher EBITDA margin than the other hotels.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give FY27 or FY28 revenue or EBITDA guidance, but said FY27 would show double-digit YoY growth and the new Convention Center should roughly double EBITDA.
Management expects ADR to reach INR 9,000-9,500 in the immediate term and close to INR 10,000 over the long run at Marriott and Courtyard, based on 5-7% organic growth plus 20-22% from refurbishment.
Management said the phase-two Marriott Hyderabad renovation (started April 2026) completes in FY27 and phase three in FY28; the overall INR 100 crore-plus programme runs in three phases.
The Convention Center renovation is targeted for completion by end-2026, with investment recovery expected in about 1.5 years.
Management said the Madhapur Courtyard (room-only model) is targeted to open in FY29 or FY30 and is in the land-conversion permission stage.
Dividend: management said the board is discussing it and expects to give a good outcome from FY28 (i.e., next year).
capex_capacity: Phase one renovation at Courtyard by Marriott Hyderabad is complete; new rooms run at 95-99% occupancy and spa revenue has more than doubled, per management.

Phase two of the Marriott Hyderabad renovation started in the first week of April 2026, with the Convention Center (now about 20,000 sq ft) under renovation from April 2026 and due for completion by end-2026.
Phase three is targeted for completion in FY28. Management said the new spa, gym and rooftop restaurant are operating.
Management said finance cost will not rise further and that cash flows and balances will fund ongoing renovation.
Management is evaluating greenfield, brownfield and distressed (NCLT) assets; expressions of interest have been shown but nothing has materialised.
demand_pricing: Management said some hotel segments saw softer occupancy and room rates in March 2026 due to the West Asia conflict and travel sentiment. Current ADRs at other businesses are close to earlier expectations, with management compensating through occupancy and outdoor catering.

Management expects demand to recover towards the wedding and corporate season at year-end and said no significant new supply is expected in the Hyderabad market over the next couple of years. Management also said supply from 2029-2030 would be absorbed by demand.
Marriott Bonvoy members account for about 65% of occupancy at the hotels, with a target of 80-85%. Management said OTA commissions are lower than for other brands.
Revenue mix at Marriott and Courtyard is about 55-60% rooms and 35-40% F&B; F&B margin is about 45-50%, with gross margin near 85%.
Seasonality: Q3 and Q4 are peak quarters, with Courtyard and Executive Apartments reaching about 90% occupancy. Portfolio occupancy is about 70% in Q1-Q2 and above 80% in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 35.3% YoY revenue growth in Q4 and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to adding Marriott Executive Apartments (75 rooms, about INR 50 crore annual revenue) from 1 January 2026. Management said the jump will not repeat, but it expects double-digit YoY growth going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Was the 183 bps margin expansion structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin gain came from the high-margin, room-led Executive Apartments and from completing renovation phase one, which upgraded back-end operations and efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the PAT decline came from depreciation versus finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline mainly to a deferred-tax benefit booked last year after the NCLT exit (eight-year loss offset window), plus extra acquisition financing; it did not split depreciation from finance cost.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ADR and RevPAR outlook and pricing strategy for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ADR fell in March but revenue budgets are protected through occupancy and outdoor catering, and ADR should recover once the wedding and corporate season returns. It also cited weekend long-stay packages and a new spa, rooftop restaurant and secretariat.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost rose from INR 64 lakh to INR 530 lakh in Q4; what is the debt plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase came from debt taken to buy Marriott Executive Apartments for about INR 215 crore, with debt previously at zero, and that no further rise in interest cost is expected. An analyst's borrowing figure was corrected on the call to INR 264 crore consolidated at 31 March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ADR growth, and how much is organic versus refurbishment-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said organic ADR growth is at least 5-7% a year, with 20-22% from refurbishment at Marriott and Courtyard, implying 25-30% overall as new inventory comes in. The immediate target is INR 9,000-9,500.

risks_watch: Softer March 2026 demand from the West Asia conflict and geopolitical tensions; ADR and occupancy recovery depends on the year-end wedding and corporate season.
Execution risk on the Convention Center (end-2026), phase two and three renovations (FY27-FY28), and Madhapur Courtyard (FY29-FY30, permissions pending).
Higher finance cost and depreciation after the INR 215 crore Executive Apartments acquisition; PAT pressure may persist.
Courtyard FY26 occupancy fell to 52.2% from 72.6%; management says it has normalised, but this needs to show in Q1 FY27 data.
Dividend timing is uncertain: management pointed only to FY28.
Management gave no formal revenue or EBITDA guidance, and the NCLT distressed-asset pipeline has not yet produced a deal.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term demand and on renovation-led margin gains, but cautious on the near term, acknowledging a softer March. It declined to give numerical guidance for FY27 or FY28, and its answers on the dividend and acquisitions were non-committal.
key_quotes: We outlined a plan to invest 100 plus crores to renovate and upgrade existing properties in three phases.
So, these three metrics, we do an in-depth analysis of the assets that's an offering and then take a call on it.
We see that in no way affecting our ADRs, and our ADRs are still going to be strongly improving because the supply will be less.
We have healthy cash revenues and healthy cash balances to fund our ongoing renovations.

growth.why: Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for FY27 (no numeric guidance) backed by renovation-driven ADR targets (INR 9,000-9,500 near term), the Convention Center twofold EBITDA uplift and Marriott Executive Apartments consolidation, but gave no FY27/FY28 numeric guidance and March demand softened.
